mechanism: Mark prior M30 high/low as a channel. Bias flips to +1/−1 only when an H1 candle fully opens and closes outside the channel; confirmation requires a subsequent full candle beyond that breakout extreme (bias_level). Trades fire only when confirmation==1 and fast EMA>slow EMA (long) or reverse (short). If price re-enters the channel, forget_bias resets and the channel recenters on the breakout candle.
data_needed: H1 OHLC; channel_high/low from M30; EMA(5) and EMA(60) on close; ATR(14) for trailing SL.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 entries; M30 channel seed; backtest 2020-01-01 to 2024-11-30
why_new_for_mis: Two-stage breakout sensor (bias then confirmation) before tagging a directional change—MIS can require full-candle outside-channel then extension beyond the breakout extreme, not a single wick pierce.
quote: When this happens, our trading strategy will have found a bias, that the markets are likely to continue moving in a particular direction. This is not the point at which our positions are entered. We will enter our positions when our bias is confirmed.

mechanism: Before committing to an EURUSD breakout, require Williams %R on EURGBP and GBPUSD on opposite sides of −50: for EURUSD longs need EURGBP WPR > −50 and GBPUSD WPR < −50 (euro strength vs GBP while dollar soft vs GBP); reverse for shorts. Treats three-way FX imbalance as a true-strength filter against false EURUSD breakouts.
data_needed: iWPR(EURGBP), iWPR(GBPUSD) on same TF as EURUSD; SymbolSelect both benchmarks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD primary; EURGBP and GBPUSD benchmarks; H1; WPR period shared
why_new_for_mis: Cross-pair WPR polarity as a triangular strength sensor for FX breakout validity—MIS can gate EURUSD regime breaks by simultaneous EUR/GBP and GBP/USD momentum imbalance.
quote: if the EURUSD price levels give us the impression that Euros are becoming more expensive than the Dollar, then we will only gain confidence if we also observe the Euro are appreciating over the Great Brutish Pound, while the Dollar is simultaneously becoming cheaper regarding the Great British Pound.

mechanism: Apply identical short period (e.g. 2–5) EMA/SMA to PRICE_OPEN and PRICE_CLOSE. Open-MA > close-MA ⇒ finishes below opens ⇒ falling/bearish tilt; close-MA > open-MA ⇒ rising/bullish tilt. Rapid re-crosses without progress flag consolidation. Same-period dual-feed MA replaces classical fast/slow period gap as the regime sensor.
data_needed: iMA(Symbol, D1, MA_PERIOD, MODE_EMA, PRICE_OPEN) and PRICE_CLOSE; optional HIGH/LOW MAs; ATR(14) for stops.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; MA_PERIOD 2; ATR 14; H1 update cadence; backtest 2020–2024
why_new_for_mis: Open-vs-close same-period MA as a low-lag directional-tilt and consolidation regime sensor—MIS gets candle-construction bias without waiting for slow/fast period separation.
quote: When the opening moving average is above the close moving average, price levels are finishing lower than they started. This is identical to knowing that price levels are falling. And the converse is true when the close moving average is above the open.

mechanism: Expand OHLC + MA(O/H/L/C) into ~40 features: horizon growth in each feed, pairwise channel spreads (O−C, O−L, H−L, …) and their lagged deltas, plus the same on MA channels. Z-score standardize; GradientBoostingRegressor / RF predicts whether the mid of MA-H and MA-L rises over HORIZON—proxy for forecasting the open/close MA crossover before it prints.
data_needed: CSV of 40 float columns; Z1/Z2 means/stds; ONNX FloatTensor [1,40]→[1,1]; HORIZON 5–10; D1 EURUSD.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; MA_PERIOD 2 SMA; train to 2023-01-29; OOS thereafter
why_new_for_mis: High-dimensional handcrafted channel-growth feature vector as an anticipatory crossover sensor—MIS can forecast mid-channel MA slope rather than wait for classical laggy crosses.
quote: a straightforward method to track this crossover is to monitor the midpoint between the two moving averages. By observing whether the midpoint has risen or fallen, we effectively capture the same information for our statistical models.

mechanism: Label Action = +1/−1 from open/close MA cross; Target = future close change over HORIZON; Reward = Target×Action; Trade Signal = 1 iff Reward>0. Train GBR/RidgeClassifier on OHLC growth + MA growth features to predict Trade Signal. Live: only take the discretionary MA-cross when model_output > 0.5—empirical high-probability setup probability.
data_needed: OHLC and MA open/close diffs over HORIZON; Action/Reward/Trade Signal labels; ONNX [1,6]→[1,1]; D1 EURUSD.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; MA_PERIOD 3 SMA; HORIZON 10; backtest 2020–2025; train cut before 2019-12-29
why_new_for_mis: Models P(strategy reward > 0 | state) instead of P(price up)—MIS can gate any rule-based signal by an empirical strategy-fitness sensor rather than raw return forecast.
quote: The probability estimated by our model, becomes the probabilities we associate with that particular signal. Hence, we can now start talking about "high probability setups" in a more scientific and empirical way

mechanism: For each bar compute Return1 = market_return × Action_MA and Return2 = market_return × Action_RSI. Targets: which strategy will be more profitable over HORIZON. LDA/MLP (~90% CV acc vs ~50% classical price direction) selects MA-cross vs RSI mid-point; EA only listens to the strategy the ONNX model expects to win.
data_needed: MA open/close (period 100 EMA), RSI(24); horizon-38 diffs; Z-scored 14 inputs; ONNX [1,14]→[2,1]; H3 EURUSD.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_H3; MA 100 EMA; RSI 24; HOLDING_PERIOD 38
why_new_for_mis: Relative strategy-win classifier as a meta-sensor—MIS can route regime attention to the currently favored rule family instead of blending correlated voters.
quote: our accuracy on the classical target is close to 50%, whereas our accuracy predicting which of the two strategies will be more profitable is around 90%

mechanism: Compute correlation matrix and rolling variance of market return vs each strategy’s transformed return. High pairwise corr (~0.75) and nearly identical risk profiles flag that the ensemble collapsed to one strategy—invalidate multi-strategy sensing until uncorrelated constituents are forced (e.g. fix vote weights=1 during optimization).
data_needed: Per-strategy Action×Return series; rolling var window=HORIZON; corr heatmap of Return/Return1/Return2.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H3; MA-cross and RSI strategies from genetic optimizer
why_new_for_mis: Strategy-return correlation / risk-identity as an ensemble-health sensor—MIS can refuse to treat correlated strategy votes as independent regime evidence.
quote: the moving average crossover and RSI strategy have a correlation of about 0.75, which is very strong. … Having two highly correlated trading strategies is effectively no better than having just one strategy

mechanism: At the start of each D1, store prior-day high/low. On first H1 bars, compare |close−last_high| vs |close−last_low|. Larger gap to prior high ⇒ bias long (day opened nearer the low); larger gap to prior low ⇒ bias short. One trade per day (rest flag); ATR(H8)×2 padding. Anticipates the day’s move without waiting for a full extreme breach.
data_needed: iHigh/iLow PERIOD_D1 shift 1; H1 close; iATR(PERIOD_H8, 4*14).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; D1 extremes; H1 entries; ~5y backtest; min lot
why_new_for_mis: Intraday opening-gap asymmetry vs prior-day range as an early daily direction/change sensor—MIS can tag expected day bias before classical high/low breakouts fire.
quote: If the day starts closer to its previous low, we go long. Conversely, if the day starts closer to its previous high, we go short.

mechanism: Two Bollinger sets, same period (20), SD=1 (inner) and SD=2 (outer). Outer-band break → mean-reversion fade (sell upper / buy lower). Inner-band break while still inside outer → trend-follow (buy above inner-high / sell below inner-low). Single indicator family emits two mutually exclusive regime modes.
data_needed: iBands×2 (BB_SD_1=2, BB_SD_2=1, period 20); ATR(14)×2 padding; D1 close.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; BB period 20; SD 1 and 2; backtest 2020–2025
why_new_for_mis: Nested dual-SD Bollinger as an explicit trend-vs-mean-reversion regime switch—MIS can tag which band family is active rather than treating all BB breaks as one state.
quote: When the inner band is broken, we interpret that as a trend-following signal; when the outer (two-standard-deviation) band is broken, we interpret that as a mean-reversion signal.

mechanism: Build corr matrix of OHLC+MA+growth features; eigendecompose. Count eigenvalues above the mean threshold as dominant market modes. Expanding-window L1 norm of corr(target, inputs) tracks non-stationary correlational strength. Rising mode count after feature enrichment signals higher regime complexity / competing modes.
data_needed: Feature matrix (17–23 cols); np.linalg.eigh on corr; expanding-window Pearson norms.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD detailed MA series CSV; train excluding last 3y; MA period 5
why_new_for_mis: Eigenvalue spectrum of the feature correlation matrix as a market-mode / regime-complexity sensor—MIS can track how many competing modes the market expresses, not only vol or trend labels.
quote: A stable market is typically governed by one dominant mode — such as a strong trend or a mean-reverting process — while a more chaotic market exhibits several competing modes.

mechanism: Train multi-output regressor to predict MA_close at horizon 1 and horizon 10 from OHLC+MA OHLC. Trade the implied slope: buy if pred_H10 > pred_H1 (and current close-MA > open-MA); sell if pred_H10 < pred_H1. Abandons comparing forecasts to live price; direction comes from forecast-to-forecast slope.
data_needed: ONNX [1,8]→[1,2] or [1,22]→[1,2]; MA O/H/L/C buffers; HORIZON=10; ATR padding.
why_new_for_mis: Implied slope between two MA forecast horizons as the directional sensor—MIS can read short-vs-long horizon MA predictions without requiring accurate absolute price forecasts.
quote: we will take our trading signals from the implied slope between the two prediction horizons. In other words— if the moving average is expected to fall across the two forecast horizons, we will sell.

mechanism: On new D1, treat engulfing as a completed 3-candle structure: prior day (1) must have lower low and higher high than day-before (2), and open_1 > open_2 for bullish (rising opens) or open_1 < open_2 for bearish. Avoids using the still-forming day-0 candle that MT5 backtests see at midnight. ATR×1.5 symmetric stops.
data_needed: iLow/iHigh/iOpen PERIOD_D1 shifts 1 and 2; ATR(14); day-stamp on TimeLocal.
why_new_for_mis: Wick-engulfing plus open-tilt on completed prior candles as a breakout/open-interest change sensor adapted to bar-open simulation—MIS can tag engulf states without look-ahead on forming bars.
quote: conditioning entries to check candle wicks instead of relying solely on open and close prices. We also found a better use for the open price: … A rising open price during an engulfing movement signaled bullish sentiment

mechanism: Classical fast(30)/slow(60) SMA cross alone is noisy. Require also low > fast MA for longs (whole candle supported above fast MA) and high < slow MA for shorts (whole candle capped under slow MA). Filters weak crosses where price is not fully on the indicated side of the average.
data_needed: iMA D1 30 and 60 SMA; daily high/low; ATR(14)×2 SL/TP.
why_new_for_mis: Candle-wick vs MA extreme concurrence as a regime-quality filter on crosses—MIS can downgrade MA-cross regimes when price wicks still violate the fast/slow side.
quote: when the low wick was above the fast moving average, we were inclined to enter long positions, and when the high wick was beneath the slow moving average, we sought to enter short positions.

mechanism: Invert classical stochastic: buy when %K > 80 and close > mid of prior-90-day high/low means; sell when %K < 20 and close < that mid. Overbought/oversold become trend-continuation tags when price sits on the matching side of the business-cycle range midpoint.
data_needed: iStochastic(D1,5,3,3); vector high/low means over 90 D1 bars; ATR(14)×2 stops.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; stochastic 5/3/3; 90-day range mid; backtest 2021–2025
why_new_for_mis: Stochastic extremes reinterpreted as trend-regime tags gated by 90-day range midpoint—MIS can run trend-follow and mean-reversion modes from the same oscillator via the mid-range side.
quote: we reinterpret the indicator as a tool for trend identification. … we first seek to enter long trades during overbought price levels. In addition, we require further confirmation by observing the close price above the midpoint of the observed high–low range.

mechanism: Add H1 filter: mean(open of last 12 H1) vs mean(close of last 12 H1). Long only if D1 stoch>80, close>90d mid, and H1 open-mean < close-mean (intraday bullish construction); short with the opposite triple. Multi-TF concurrence for trend-change entries.
data_needed: D1 stochastic + 90d mid; H1 open/close vectors length 12; ATR D1.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 stochastic regime; H1 12-bar open/close means; 2021–2025
why_new_for_mis: Lower-TF open/close mean tilt as a concurrence sensor on HTF stochastic trend tags—MIS can require D1 extreme + range mid + H1 candle-construction agreement before change events.
quote: a trend observed on the daily time frame should also be reflected in the spread between the open and close prices on a lower time frame

mechanism: Z-score OHLC+BB(upper/mid/lower)+RSI; RandomForest multi-output predicts future BB upper/mid/lower and RSI. Sell if classical BB+RSI overbought OR (forecast RSI < current RSI AND forecast BB mid < current BB mid); buy on the bullish dual. Forecasted indicator slopes expand rare classical BB+RSI confluence signals.
data_needed: ONNX [1,8]→[1,4]; Z1/Z2 floats; iBands(30,SD2), iRSI(15); D1 EURUSD; HORIZON 5.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 main, H4 trading stamp; BB 30/2; RSI 15; backtest 2023–2026
why_new_for_mis: Joint forecast of BB-mid slope and RSI direction as an ensemble regime/change sensor that densifies sparse classical BB+RSI extremes—MIS can synthesize indicator-path forecasts into tradeable state tags.
quote: new trading rules were introduced that combined forecasted RSI direction and the forecasted slope of the middle Bollinger Band with the original trading signal we started with.
